correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the proof from the frozen Finding and Proof. Conflicting incoming or outgoing arcs have disjoint supporter sets and so cannot both meet 2q>r. Relative to any spanning path the only possible extra union arc is its closing arc. In the cycle case each order omits one arc, quorum bounds the omissions by c=r-q, and the union recovers the cycle, precluding multiple counting. For s occupied cut sites the positive bounded allocation exists iff s<=r<=sc; this proves both the census and the full diversity spectrum, including exclusion of diversity two. For n=1 or c=0 the cyclic coefficient vanishes. For q<=r/2 the two specified order types with multiplicities q and r-q support every used arc but give branching even after appending a common suffix. The inspected checker enumerates finite order tuples independently of the coefficient DP; it was not executed. The universal results here are proved combinatorially, not by the finite census.

value.rationale: Quorum is a natural local agreement condition on named linear successors. The theorem turns it into a complete global classification, an exact labelled count and a sharp threshold for how many distinct orders can coexist. It explains why two distinct orders cannot occur as the only types and why this rigidity fails right at half quorum. The substantive result is the structural package, not the standard allocation identity by itself.
